_purpose: The failure behaviour, which matters more than the happy path: a mistyped parameter name, a wrongly-typed value, a value outside a declared enum, and an asset path that resolves to nothing are all refused rather than quietly ignored. Each step asserts its own refusal with expect_failure, so the reason is checked per step instead of read by eye.
_reading: These steps pass BY being refused. A step that succeeds is the bug: it means the tool ran with a default in place of what was asked for, and reported on work it did not do.
_history: Until step params were validated inside run_scenario, none of this was actually tested. The validator had one call site - the HTTP transport - so a scenario step went straight to the tool with whatever it was given: the mistyped 'parent' below was dropped in silence and bp_create made an Actor, and the step passed. The unknown-tool case that used to live here refused the whole file at parse time, so these steps never ran at all; it is now 18-unknown-tool.json.

steps._note: Mistyped name. The real parameter is parent_class; 'parent' must be refused with the suggestion, not ignored in favour of the default parent.
Wrong type. A number sent as a string must be refused before the tool coerces it and reports confidently on the wrong count.
Outside the declared enum. edit_history accepts list|undo|redo, and anything else must be named as such rather than falling through to a default action.
A path that resolves to nothing is refused rather than accepted as null.

teardown._note: Proves the first step really was refused. If bp_create had run, this would find the asset it should never have made.
